standard_prerequisites.name: Encode-decode data for a pointed type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A fibration code:A->type with code(x) a k-type, a point c0:code(a0), a decoding map decode and the two round-trip identifications.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the hypotheses of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation recursion and induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map out of trunc k (id a0 x) may be defined by recursion when its target is a k-type, and a k-type indexed goal may be proved by induction on the truncation.
standard_prerequisites.use: The encode map is defined by recursion and the second round-trip is proved by induction.

standard_prerequisites.name: k-type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is a k-type when all its path types are trivial above level k; in particular paths in a k-type form a k-type.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reason the truncation induction of the proof is allowed, and the reason the recursion defining encode is legitimate.

core_obligations: Read off decode composed with encode as the identity directly from the third hypothesis, which states that identification for all c:code(a0) (source line 2635).

For the other composite, do a truncation induction, legitimate because paths in a k-type are a k-type, reducing the goal to showing decode of encode of the truncated path equals that path (source lines 2637-2642).
Do a path induction on that goal, reduce encode by its recursion rule, and conclude with the fourth hypothesis (source lines 2643-2644).

proof_roadmap.step: The composite decode after encode is the identity by hypothesis (iii).
Reduce encode after decode to a family over paths by truncation induction, using that paths in a k-type are a k-type.
Path induction on the truncated path, reduce encode by its recursion rule and apply hypothesis (iv).

The author gave it no label, so its first-edition position is part of its identity.
